title: Non-Monotonic Dynamical Correlations Across The Glass Crossover
authors: Corentin C. L. Laudicina, Ilian Pihlajamaa, Liesbeth M. C. Janssen, Thomas Voigtmann, Tommaso Rizzo
abstract: The dramatic slowing down of structural relaxation in supercooled liquids is accompanied by the emergence of dynamic heterogeneity. A monotonically increasing dynamical correlation length, measured at the $α$-timescale, is one of the remarkable features of this phenomenon. Here we show that this picture is incomplete: the dynamical correlation length measured in the $β$-relaxation regime exhibits a striking non-monotonic temperature dependence, reaching a maximum near the mode-coupling crossover temperature $T_c$ and decreasing upon further cooling, even as local dynamical fluctuations continue to intensify. This behavior suggests a crossover from spatially extended, maximally cooperative motion near $T_c$ to increasingly compact and localized relaxation events below it. We demonstrate that this evolution is quantitatively captured by stochastic beta-relaxation theory, an extension of mode-coupling theory beyond mean-field that explicitly predicts an avoided dynamical transition in finite dimensions. Our results provide the first direct spatial evidence in favor of the avoided-transition picture of the mode-coupling crossover, and establish the peak of the $β$-regime correlation length as a robust indicator of the mode-coupling crossover.
summary: This work reveals that the dynamical correlation length in supercooled liquids exhibits non-monotonic behavior in the $ eta$-relaxation regime across the glass crossover temperature ($T_c$). By extending Mode-Coupling Theory, the authors provide direct spatial evidence supporting an avoided dynamical transition picture, suggesting a fundamental change in the nature of local particle motion below $T_c$.
main_problem: The study investigates the temperature dependence of the dynamical correlation length across the glass crossover temperature ($T_c$), challenging the assumption that dynamics are only governed by $\alpha$-relaxation.
main_result: The dynamical correlation length in the $ eta$-relaxation regime shows a striking non-monotonic dependence, peaking near $T_c$ and decreasing upon further cooling, indicating a crossover from extended to localized motion.
method: The analysis uses molecular dynamics simulations combined with stochastic $ eta$-relaxation theory, extending Mode-Coupling Theory (MCT) beyond mean-field predictions.
model_or_system: The system studied is a supercooled liquid, modeled in both two and three dimensions, exhibiting structural relaxation dynamics.
key_observables: Dynamical correlation length ($\xi_d(t)$), Overlap function $Q(t)$, and the spatially resolved mobility field $\mu(\mathbf{r}, t)$.
important_parameters: The mode-coupling crossover temperature ($T_c$), the $ eta$-relaxation regime, and the dimensionality ($d=2, 3$).
main_assumptions: The theory relies on stochastic $ eta$-relaxation theory to capture the avoided dynamical transition predicted beyond mean-field MCT.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two-step decay of the overlap function $Q(t)$ across $T_c$ and spatial maps of the mobility field $\mu(\mathbf{r}, t)$ showing heterogeneous structures.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the anomalous non-monotonic behavior of $\xi_d$ in the $ eta$-regime, contrasting it with previous $\alpha$-regime studies. It then develops the theoretical framework using stochastic $ eta$-relaxation theory to quantitatively capture this crossover, providing spatial evidence for the avoided-transition picture.
why_interesting: The focus on non-equilibrium dynamics, glassy physics, and the extension of mean-field theories (MCT) to capture finite-dimensional effects is highly relevant to understanding complex, slow dynamics in many-body quantum systems.
